name: Brain Network (hard)
description: Breaking news from zombie neurology! It turns out that – contrary to previous beliefs – every zombie is born with a single brain, and only later it evolves into a complicated brain structure. In fact, whenever a zombie consumes a brain, a new brain appears in its nervous system and gets immediately connected to one of the already existing brains using a single brain connector. Researchers are now interested in monitoring the brain latency of a zombie. Your task is to write a program which, given a history of evolution of a zombie's nervous system, computes its brain latency at every stage.
input_specification: The first line of the input contains one number n – the number of brains in the final nervous system ( 2 ≤ n ≤ 200000 ). In the second line a history of zombie's nervous system evolution is given. For convenience, we number all the brains by 1, 2, ..., n in the same order as they appear in the nervous system (the zombie is born with a single brain, number 1 , and subsequently brains 2, 3, ..., n are added). The second line contains n - 1 space-separated numbers p 2 , p 3 , ..., p n , meaning that after a new brain k is added to the system, it gets connected to a parent-brain .
output_specification: Output n - 1 space-separated numbers – the brain latencies after the brain number k is added, for k = 2, 3, ..., n .
approach_summary: Precompute 2^k ancestor jumps up[u][k] and node depths in O(N log N). Compute LCA and path aggregates in O(log N) per query.
